national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of 15-year-old students in Bosnia and Herzegovina who have not attained Level 2, the basic proficiency level, on the PISA scale in reading, mathematics and science. Lower indicator values indicate a more favourable outcome.
national_rationale: The data come from the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), an international survey conducted by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to assess the knowledge and skills of 15-year-old students. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the preparation and implementation of the 2018 survey were coordinated by the Agency for Pre-primary, Primary and Secondary Education (APOSO), in cooperation with the competent education authorities. The results show the share of students who have not attained Level 2 in each of the three domains.
national_methodology_characteristics: The national data refer to the results of the 2018 PISA survey. Bosnia and Herzegovina did not participate in the 2022 PISA cycle; therefore, a continuous time series for monitoring changes in student performance is currently unavailable. International comparability is based on the common methodology and standardised procedures of the PISA survey. Due to the lack of comparable data from multiple cycles, progress status cannot be calculated at the national level.
national_long_objective: The long-term objective is to improve the quality of education in Bosnia and Herzegovina and reduce the share of 15-year-old students who do not attain the basic proficiency level in reading, mathematics and science. Continued participation in international assessments such as PISA is important for monitoring educational outcomes and identifying areas requiring improvement. No specific quantified national target has been established for this indicator.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of 15-year-old students who have not attained Level 2 (the basic proficiency level) on the PISA scale in three domains: reading, mathematics and science. The data come from the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), an international survey that assesses the knowledge and skills of 15-year-old students.
eu_rationale: The data are collected through the PISA survey conducted by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The indicator shows the share of 15-year-old students who have not attained Level 2 on the proficiency scale in each of the three domains. PISA is conducted in multi-year cycles, and its results enable international comparisons of educational outcomes and monitoring of student performance.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers 15-year-old students enrolled in at least the seventh grade of education. Level 2 represents the basic proficiency level on the PISA scale, and students who do not attain it are considered low achievers. Data are available for reading, mathematics and science, enabling comparisons between countries and monitoring of changes across PISA cycles. Lower indicator values represent a more favourable outcome.
eu_long_objective: Improving students’ basic knowledge and skills is one of the priorities of the European Education Area. In accordance with the Council Resolution on the second cycle of the Strategic Framework for European Cooperation in Education and Training for the period 2026–2030, a common EU target has been set for the share of 15-year-old students with low achievement in reading, mathematics and science to be below 15% by 2030. The target applies to each of the three domains and represents a common EU reference target, not an individual target value for each Member State.
